messages.subject: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.

The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:

library("RMySQL")

con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)

sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")

results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)

dbDisconnect(con)

The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.

If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.

I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:

system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))

I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.

I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.

I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.

However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:

Error in .local(drv, ...) :
  Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)

Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.

If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.

I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
Can you configure your mysql server to have port 3306 open to the following IP addresses? These are the addresses your app may be running from. That would allow you to connect from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers to your remote MySQL server.
54.204.37.78

54.204.29.251

54.204.36.75

54.204.34.9

If you can’t do that, port forwarding could work. That will allow you to connect to your mysql server as if its running locally (of course it actually wouldn’t be). Something like
ssh -nNTL 3306:localhost:3306 username@hostname
That command won’t exit (unless the connection is broken), so you’ll prob need to run it as a background process (which you can do in R or add an ampersand (&) to the end of the ssh command.

Hope that helps
​

On Sun, Feb 1, 2015 at 10:41 AM, Phill Clarke <phill...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
>
> The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
>
> results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
>
> If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
>
> I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
>
> system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
>
> I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
>
> I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
>
> I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
>
> However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
>
> Error in .local(drv, ...) :
>   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
>
> Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
>
> If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
>
> I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
>
>
>
>

Hello,

I am trying to deploy a Shiny app but am running into a few errors. The first is that I get a warning about an absolute path in my file:
>> Question 1: do I need to use the ~ notation in the directories in order for the app to deploy properly on the server? I am loading in an .Rdata file from the data folder within the project directory, which is why I define a working directory.

The second issue is a parsing manifest error. Originally, I had a number of other project-related (but not Shiny-related) files in the folder, but realized it was causing the app deployment to load unnecessary documents. I therefore moved all non-Shiny files out of the project directory, including ke_profile.xlsx. However, this file is being referenced in the error message below with "checksum mismatch."

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Will Shiny remove the option for private apps on the free plan?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Will Shiny remove the option for private apps on the free plan?
messages.body_plain:
Absolutely not, that would be terrible. :)  The flow will be the following:

At the time of general availability, everyone using the service will be notified that they will have seven days to select which plan they are interested in.

After seven days, If no action is taken to select a plan, the account will be placed into the free tier.  All applications that have authentication turned on, will be terminated so as to avoid them loading without authentication.  If a customer decides that they would like to turn authentication on, they would need to upgrade to the starter tier to do so.

Please let us know if you have any other questions or suggestions.

Best,
Tareef

messages.subject: lubridate depends on locale, C locale only available on shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: lubridate depends on locale, C locale only available on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
I need to parse a date string in my shiny app (from a unix log file). I'm using the lubridate library to parse date strings.
When the date string has a month name it depends on the locale to parse it. Shinyapps.io seems to have only the C locale and therefore fails to parse a string like "2015 Jan 8".
I've not been able to set the locale to something else.

I've created an example to demonstrate this
runGist("d5915f1415ca2663068f")

This may or may not work on your local setup depending on your locale. If you have an english locale it will work.
But on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> this will fail

Any ideas how I can get this to work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>?

messages.subject: shinyapps.io: the server responded with a status of 500
messages.subject_clean: shinyapps.io: the server responded with a status of 500
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm developing an app that no longer seems to work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> (see below for details). The app works as expected when I run it locally on my computer. I had it working last night on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, this morning I woke up, changed two lines of code, redeployed the app, and now it seems to be having issues. I have also tried rolling back to the version I had working last night, and re-deploying that version on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> but I still encounter the same issue.

Specifically, the issue seems to be that instances have trouble loading js and css files stored in the www directory. The javascript console in Google Chrome yields the message 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 (Internal Server Error)' error for several files (I have attached a screenshot below).

A post on SO (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26110445/shinyapps-io-failed-to-load-resource-the-server-responded-with-a-status-of-500) indicates that this might be occur if the total memory required to run the app exceeds a certain threshold. However, the proposed solution of changing the allocated size to 'xlarge' or 'xxlarge' does not work for me. But even if the changes between last nights' version and this morning's version pushed the total memory required above some limit, and even if 'xlarge' and 'xxlarge' are not available for a free user, I would have expected rolling back to the previous working to have fix. I have also tried copying the directory, removing  .git folder, and redeploying from the new directory in case the .git folder was getting uploaded to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and a change in the .git folder caused the total size to eclipse a threshold, but this did not work either.

I was wondering if anyone had any ideas on what's happening, and if there were any changes at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> during the last 15 hours or so?

Cheers,

Jeff

---------------------------------------------

The app is deployed at:

https://paleo13.shinyapps.io/mapotron/

The app is on github at (note that several files containing passwords and tokens are not present):

https://github.com/paleo13/mapotron/tree/dropbox-backup

Note that it uses a fork of leaflet-shiny:

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Unable to connect to local database after deploying the app on Shinyapps.io, HELP!
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Unable to connect to local database after deploying the app on Shinyapps.io, HELP!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,
The problem is that your application is looking to connect to a database on local host.  You probably have a database running on your own machine, but Shinyapps.io doesn't have your database.  You will need to either open a connection to your database from the outside world, bundle the data you are pulling out of the DB into CSV or RData files, or move your database to a service that can be reached remotely.

Hope this helps.

messages.body_plain:
You should be able to take his code out of a function and turn it into single-file app:
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/single-file.html

If you want to keep the function, the app.R file could simply call the function at the end:

======================
myapp <- function() {
  ...
  shinyApp(ui, server)
}

# Call myapp() so that app.R returns the shiny app object
myapp()
======================

-Winston

Further, I have never been able to connect from my ipad.  In checking the dashboard, an instance does seem to start running but app never loads on the ipad, just "please wait."

Are there some usage concepts in the free version I am missing? I would like to invite others to try the app.

Is there a way to ensure the connection ceases when the browser window is closed?

Thanks.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Arthur,
I tried your application right now but of course it loaded instantaneously on my computer, ipad and iphone  :)  It would be great if you see the interminable wait to send us a note immediately, you should not be seeing that at all.
Closing a browser window should definitely close the connection, are you seeing any data to indicate that is not happening?  There are timeouts that you can set that will close a connection even if the browser tab is open if the connection has been idle for some time.

As for the timeouts, which timeouts did you set?  Given the usage graph on your application, it definitely looks like your application gets started on a daily basis, but I am wondering now whether there are conditions under which the iPad browser won't correctly route to the application if the application was sleeping.  You could test that by stopping the instance, and trying to hit the application from a web browser on your computer first, stopping the instance again, and trying to hit the application from a web browser on your ipad.

Looking forward to figuring out why Godot isn't showing up :)
-Tareef

messages.subject: Tier limits in Beta ETA? And pricing questions in general
messages.subject_clean: Tier limits in Beta ETA? And pricing questions in general
messages.body_plain:
Hello!  Thanks for a great package.

I deployed something this weekend which got popular on twitter, so I'm already at 20 hours after a day.  I would like to keep the app running but would like to check if the app will suddenly get turned off at some point when I hit the limit.  The previous post said maybe Feb for the end of beta, so that's obviously anytime now.

I'm also a bit torn about the pricing structure, as if say the app stays popular and its used 24 hours per day, thats 720 Active Hours which needs a $99 a month plan which is way beyond my budget without charging people for using the app. A more realistic 16 hours a day we are around the 500 hours a month mark, but this is still $39 a month

Would I even be allowed to charge others for use under the TOS?

At that pricing level it may make more sense for me to spin up a Shiny Server on private hosting? I see Digital Ocean have a 0.5 GB RAM server for $5 a month, is this equivalent to your medium tier?

Ideally for me (and realise this is not my business so expect you to not agree :) ) I'd like a package like Basic but with the Active Hours all bumped up and say the number of allowed apps taken down.  Perhaps also the tiers only allowed to be small/medium on the lower price plans.  Say $25 a month if you pay annually, 500 Active Hours and 10 apps allowed.

Anyhow, I only suggest above because I love the product and want to keep using it, so please take it all as constructive feedback as intended.

Yours sincerely,
Mark

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Tier limits in Beta ETA? And pricing questions in general
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Tier limits in Beta ETA? And pricing questions in general
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the constructive feedback Mark, we really appreciate it.
You had several questions here, hopefully I got to all of them:
- when is beta ending
We are still tracking for the end of Feb, we will announce general availability and then everyone will have a week to get to the plan that makes the most sense to them.

- regarding the number of hours of usage
Our data suggests that the vast majority of accounts and apps have a usage pattern that should fit well with the free and starter tier.  That being said we will only be stopping apps from loading if they are in the free tier.  We won't be charging any overages for extra hours in the paid plans until we learn more about our hour allotments.  We have heard your suggestion before and it is definitely on the docket of consideration.

- charging for your apps
You absolutely should be able to charge for your apps, nothing (hopefully) in our TOS should prevent that. Please let me know which lines led you to feel that way.

- digital ocean and running your own server
I am not super familiar with Digital Ocean's infrastructure but some of our engineers have used it and love it.   The key you have to consider is around the management and monitoring of your application.  If 0.5GB of Ram is sufficient for all your applications then that might be a radically inexpensive option assuming you are okay with the management/monitoring overhead.  A single R process takes 50MB up front. ShinyApps.io allows you to have different RAM allocations on a per application basis. We take care of distributing the application across servers and of course you can scale the number of instances and the amount of Ram and the number of R processes per application.

I hope I got all your questions. Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Thanks for your help and suggestions Mark, we really appreciate it and the kind words.

Tareef

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Gray Screen
messages.body_plain:
Carrie,

This could be related to two things. First, depending on how many users are using your application simultaneously, you could be running out of memory. This is possible if your application uses large amounts of memory for each user session. To address this, you could try increasing your application instance size in the application settings page, or by using the configureApp() function of the shinyapps package.

Second this could be related to the 'Worker Connection Timeout' setting on the application settings page (under Advanced). This setting controls how long a session is allowed to be idle before it is closed. Idle session refer to sessions where the broswer tab is open but not being used. You can increase this setting if you wish (however it should be noted that you still consume instance hours even when a session is idle).

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Apologies it's taken me a while to reply to this, but I have it figured out.

My solution looks like this:

# Load db connector library

library("RMySQL")

# SSH

system(paste("sshpass -p 'remotesyspassword' ssh -f -L 3306:localhost:3306 username@remotsystemhostname sleep 20"))

# Open MySQL connection

con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host='127.0.0.1', user='mysqlusername', password='mysqlpassword', dbname='databasename')

# MySQL Query

sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.databasetable", sep="")

fbRacecard <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)

# Close MySQL connection

dbDisconnect(con)

On Sunday, 1 February 2015 15:41:40 UTC, Phill Clarke wrote:
> I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
>
> The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
>
> results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
>
> If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
>
> I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
>
> system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
>
> I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
>
> I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
>
> I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
>
> However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
>
> Error in .local(drv, ...) :
>   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
>
> Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
>
> If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
>
> I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
>
>
>
>

On Monday, 16 February 2015 20:32:31 UTC+1, Tareef Kawaf wrote:

> Thank you for the constructive feedback Mark, we really appreciate it.
> You had several questions here, hopefully I got to all of them:
> - when is beta ending
> We are still tracking for the end of Feb, we will announce general availability and then everyone will have a week to get to the plan that makes the most sense to them.
>
> - regarding the number of hours of usage
> Our data suggests that the vast majority of accounts and apps have a usage pattern that should fit well with the free and starter tier.  That being said we will only be stopping apps from loading if they are in the free tier.  We won't be charging any overages for extra hours in the paid plans until we learn more about our hour allotments.  We have heard your suggestion before and it is definitely on the docket of consideration.
>
> - charging for your apps
> You absolutely should be able to charge for your apps, nothing (hopefully) in our TOS should prevent that. Please let me know which lines led you to feel that way.
>
> - digital ocean and running your own server
> I am not super familiar with Digital Ocean's infrastructure but some of our engineers have used it and love it.   The key you have to consider is around the management and monitoring of your application.  If 0.5GB of Ram is sufficient for all your applications then that might be a radically inexpensive option assuming you are okay with the management/monitoring overhead.  A single R process takes 50MB up front. ShinyApps.io allows you to have different RAM allocations on a per application basis. We take care of distributing the application across servers and of course you can scale the number of instances and the amount of Ram and the number of R processes per application.
>
> I hope I got all your questions. Please let me know if you have any other questions.
>
> Thanks for your help and suggestions Mark, we really appreciate it and the kind words.
>
> Tareef

> On Monday, February 16, 2015, Mark Edmondson <m...@markedmondson.me> wrote:

> > Hello!  Thanks for a great package.
> >
> > I deployed something this weekend which got popular on twitter, so I'm already at 20 hours after a day.  I would like to keep the app running but would like to check if the app will suddenly get turned off at some point when I hit the limit.  The previous post said maybe Feb for the end of beta, so that's obviously anytime now.
> >
> > I'm also a bit torn about the pricing structure, as if say the app stays popular and its used 24 hours per day, thats 720 Active Hours which needs a $99 a month plan which is way beyond my budget without charging people for using the app. A more realistic 16 hours a day we are around the 500 hours a month mark, but this is still $39 a month
> >
> > Would I even be allowed to charge others for use under the TOS?
> >
> > At that pricing level it may make more sense for me to spin up a Shiny Server on private hosting? I see Digital Ocean have a 0.5 GB RAM server for $5 a month, is this equivalent to your medium tier?
> >
> > Ideally for me (and realise this is not my business so expect you to not agree :) ) I'd like a package like Basic but with the Active Hours all bumped up and say the number of allowed apps taken down.  Perhaps also the tiers only allowed to be small/medium on the lower price plans.  Say $25 a month if you pay annually, 500 Active Hours and 10 apps allowed.
> >
> > Anyhow, I only suggest above because I love the product and want to keep using it, so please take it all as constructive feedback as intended.
> >
> > Yours sincerely,
> > Mark

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajarshi,
It looks like you have an error in your shiny application.  Typically what I have found is that usually there is some data that you are loading properly in your local environment, that isn't part of the application when you deployed it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
One way to validate that, would be to restart your R process and see if the application runs well.  If you are loading data from a file, I would check to mamke sure that the file you are loading is in the same directory (or a directory below) the one containing ui.R and server.R

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] How can I destroy or delete an archived application
messages.body_plain:
As others have noted, the ability to delete an app is necessary. Lack of the delete capability is a show-stopper defect for me.

On Friday, January 9, 2015 at 7:33:58 AM UTC-8, Etienne Laurin wrote:
> Greetings,
>
> Do you not feel that the lack of this option could impact the viability of the business?
> Corporations have obligations and some include the complete destruction of certain informations. Not archiving. If they feel that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> cannot comply with the rules they have to follow, they may not come onboard.
>
> Le jeudi 8 janvier 2015 13:17:18 UTC-5, Tareef Kawaf a écrit :
> > Thanks for the feedback Dieter,
> > it is definitely on our list of work to do, and we recognize its importance but we felt that getting more feedback on the viability of the business behind shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> was a higher priority.  The complete implementation of delete is a little more involved and we wanted to tackle it holistically.  To be clear on what the "Security issue" risk is here is more about RStudio conceivably going to look at an application and its data.   There is no way to serve an archived app, and everything related to the application is segmented by account with strict permissioning.  It isn't clear just how prevalent the need for delete is versus some of the other missing capabilities in the platform which are more widely applicable to the larger audience.

messages.subject_clean: R script working locally; not working on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to put together a R + Shiny app that, at least initially, plots a histogram of date data. I have it working just fine on my local system in RStudio, but in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> it doesn't work.

I've posted this question (and the code) on stackoverflow (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28656683/r-script-working-locally-not-working-on-shinyapp-io) but noone's suggested an answer yet.

The app, at the moment, is very simple - the user interface doesn't really do anything, and the data is just a small sample of test data.

Works fine in RStudio (draws a nice little histogram). When loaded on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the 'title panel' text and sidebar display but after a second or two either it - reports the error "'from' cannot be NA, NaN or infinite" or - the screen greys out and the script stops (?) in both cases without producing a histogram.

Has me baffled; would be interested to hear if anyone has any suggestions for where I've gone wrong.

Cheers,
Nik

I am trying a simple Shiny -2- SQL connection example.

I have a UI where user enters a number (in this case ID #). Shiny then sends this to a SQL Query and then results from the Query are displayed back on the UI screen.

UI.r
  shinyUI(fluidPage(
    titlePanel("Test Case"),
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel((""),
             textInput("mrnnumb", "Enter ID number",""),
             submitButton("Ok")),
      mainPanel(("Results"),
         tableOutput("dis"))
)
))
server.r
 library(RODBC)
 library(sqldf)
 myconn = odbcConnect("Test1", uid="12345", pwd="password123")

 shinyServer(function(input, output) {

 a1 = reactive({input$mrnnumb})

 testq =  reactive({ sqlQuery(myconn, paste("select DOB,GenderCode,MaritalStatus,IDNumber from Demographics_extended where IDNumber = '",a1,"'"))})

 output$dis<-renderDataTable(testq)

 })

The results are null...nothing is happening....no error..no message...nothing....Need some help

Shiny Cool

messages.body_plain:
Nik,

Dates could be affected by locale settings on the system, and that's why you see a different behavior on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. To get around that (besides the solution that Paul provided), you could set the locale to "C" in your code, something like this:

    orig_locale <- Sys.getlocale("LC_TIME")
    Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C")
    text_date <- c("9 March 2006", "31 October 2008", "24 September 2008", "27 February 2009", "19 May 2014", "11 December 2009", "7 August 2013", "8 December 2014", "2 February 2010", "22 December 2014", "20 December 2011", "4 September 2009", "19 December 2013", "10 October 2007", "19 September 2008")
    num_date <- as.Date(text_date, format = "%d %B %Y")
    Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", orig_locale)

Fereshteh

If you visit the URL that you provided (with the lower case a), you could be hitting a bug where application names are case in-sensitive, but URLs are treated case sensitively. The workaround is to always ensure you have the "correct" URL.

-Andy

We aren't typically setup to analyze R code, but I believe that what is happening here is that .indexwday is being impacted by the timezone that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> runs in. messages.subject: Re: file dependency problem in shinyapps
messages.subject_clean: file dependency problem in shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
(add shinyapps-users, remove shiny-discuss)

Wow, bizarre:

> This function uses the MaxEnt species distribution model software, which is a java program that you can download here. Put the file ’maxent.jar’ in the ’java’ folder of this package. That is the folder returned by system.file("java", package="dismo"). You need MaxEnt version 3.3.3b or higher. Please note that this program (maxent.jar) cannot be redistributed or used for commercial or for-profit purposes.

You could try including that jar file in the root directory of your app, then in global.R copy the file from "maxent.jar" to system.file("java/maxent.jar", package="dismo"). But I wouldn't be surprised if it fails to copy due to permissions. It would be easy if the dismo package could provide an option that lets you provide your own location for maxent.jar.
